definitions.meaning: weather that is fair to an adequate degree: fair means clear and bright, enough means adequately
a phrase of acceptance, conceding a point is reasonable

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: FAIR is clear weather, and ENOUGH stands for 'reasonably'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a spoken concession meaning 'all right', and read literally it describes weather that is adequately bright.

clue.text: Cover boundary position that's under attack

parts.note: a front is a cover or facade hiding something
a line marks a boundary

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at cover or the boundary feels exposed to the batsman's attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' and 'boundary' look like cricket fielding positions, which makes 'position' seem part of the same picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops nearest the enemy hold the most exposed position in a battle, the one facing attack.

clue.text: Flag is in for repair, I see

indicators.note: the answer is sitting in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A flag has been sent in for mending, someone remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but it is the plant, the yellow flag being a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag is a common name for a wild plant of this genus with sword-shaped leaves.

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: outlandish means bizarre, so the letters are set out strangely

explanation.surface: Bizarre designs make someone nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlandish' rearranges DESIGNS into DGINESS, which follows E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge, nervy and tense, is a state of worry.

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the pole's letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: sombre means dark and dull
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: A card game is described as tedious once a Polish player has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is a magnetic pole, S for south, removed from SOMBRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is an old three-handed trick-taking game played with cards, popular in the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Wake up call for Walter Mitty?

definitions.text: Wake up call for Walter Mitty?

parts.words: Wake up call for Walter Mitty?
parts.note: Walter Mitty is the daydreaming fantasist of a James Thurber story, so the call is telling a dreamer to face facts

explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty, from James Thurber's story, lives in heroic daydreams; the phrase that would rouse him is a blunt command to be realistic.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an impatient instruction to stop fantasising and accept reality, exactly what a daydreamer needs to hear.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the expectations word goes round the leader's letter

parts.note: prospects are expectations of the future

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Hopes centre on a trade union chief's published programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PROSPECTS around U, the first letter of 'union', giving PROSPECT-U-S.
explanation.definitionFit: A document setting out a company's or college's aims and offer is a kind of published declaration.

indicators.note: fluttering means moving about agitatedly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bird flits about in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' rearranges GARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A male goose is a farmyard bird.

indicators.note: foolish means silly, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A grandmother making a silly racket is being quarrelsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolish' rearranges NOISE and GRAN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting out a case logically is a sense of making an argument.

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: Just an American lagging behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like 'lagging', but it is the noun: in American English the word for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang this is the buttocks, a person's rear end.

clue.text: Unruffled by head of state's key appointment

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: E is a musical key
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: A minister stays calm after a senior state post is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like a president, but it gives S, the first letter of 'state'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and composed, with nothing disturbing one's poise.

explanation.walkthrough: 'from' links the two senses; neither 'engagement' to marry nor money paid is meant directly.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is advantage or good, the other is the involvement of being absorbed in something.

clue.text: Marked out artist accompanying several on tour

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the marked word is placed around the others

parts.note: telling means marked or striking, as in a telling difference
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
V is five in Roman numerals, standing loosely for several

explanation.surface: An artist who stood out is going on tour with a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts TELLING around RA and V: T-RA-V-ELLING. V, the Roman five, stands for 'several' here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on tour is journeying from place to place.

clue.text: Try to catch attention — switch on

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' means placed after the preceding piece

parts.note: an ear is attention, as in 'lend an ear'
a switch is a tress of false hair, a wig

explanation.surface: Someone grabs notice and flicks the power on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' looks like a power switch, but it is a hairpiece. To earwig is to try to overhear.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to strain to overhear what others say, an informal British verb.

clue.text: Allies regrouping around a British queen

indicators.note: around means the reordered letters go round the others
regrouping means forming into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The Allies reform their lines around a British monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regrouping' turns ALLIES into ISELLA, and 'around' puts it round A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Several queens bore this name, among them the Spanish monarch who backed Columbus and the wife of Edward II.

parts.note: the line is a railway line, and the provider serves food on a train rather than on the internet

explanation.walkthrough: 'On line' looks like 'online', the internet; it is a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage serving light meals provides refreshments while the train is on the line.

clue.text: Bob's successful at first, winning prize draw

indicators.note: at first means this piece comes before the other in the word

parts.note: lucky means fortunate, successful by chance
a bob is a dip, a quick bob or duck down

explanation.surface: Bob succeeded at the first attempt, coming out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is a quick downward movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub of wrapped prizes into which people plunge a hand to win something random is a fairground game.

clue.text: Aesthetically pleasing flat set off with hint of ultramarine

indicators.note: off means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
a hint is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A flat is decorated with a touch of deep blue to look good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges FLAT, SET and U, the first letter of 'ultramarine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing good judgement in style, so attractive to look at.

clue.text: Comfort fall guy, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this signals the word spoken sounds the same as the answer

parts.note: a sucker is a dupe, someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: Consoling the man who takes the blame, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: SUCKER, a fall guy, sounds like the word for help and comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid given in hardship is support and solace.

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
the tonic is the keynote, the first note of a scale

explanation.surface: An old man's drink of tonic is famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tonic' looks like a drink, but it is the musical keynote.
explanation.definitionFit: Noteworthy and distinguished, deserving recognition.

clue.text: Ring order in to deliver flowering plant

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the order goes inside the deliverance word

parts.note: to rid is to free or deliver, as in 'rid of'
CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order

explanation.surface: Telephone in an order to have a flowering plant delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like phoning, but it is the letter O. CH, the Order of the Companions of Honour, goes in RID.
explanation.definitionFit: These exotic blooms belong to a large family of plants with showy flowers.

parts.note: read as ill humour, comedy in poor taste, not a bad temper

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-humour' usually means bad temper; read here as tasteless comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tasteless jest about suffering or disaster is humour that is distasteful.

clue.text: Obscure fictional character securing good try

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the character encloses the letter

parts.note: Jude the Obscure is Thomas Hardy's novel

explanation.surface: An obscure character in a novel gets a good attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' is part of the title of Hardy's novel Jude the Obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear a case in court is to try it.

clue.text: No end to money the Italian writer's got

indicators.note: having no end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: pence are coins, money
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian author has an endless supply of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end to' drops the final E of PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is an implement for writing.

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read backwards from bottom to top

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Catch up on the part you're playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PART round, which reads upward in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is a device for catching animals.

indicators.note: overcome read as turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: doom is disaster, ruin

explanation.surface: Sense that catastrophe must be defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome' looks like 'defeated', but here it means turned over: DOOM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of mind or temper is an emotional state.

explanation.walkthrough: 'to reach' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the course something is pointed along; the other is the supervision of people or a project.

parts.note: a village common is a green, so read as a policy document for the common

explanation.walkthrough: A UK government discussion paper on proposed policy is named after its cover's colour; 'Common' is a village green.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a government consultation paper setting out proposals is named after its colour.
